scenes.visual: Title card 'Changing the Cause on Purpose' fades in over a cartoon mountain stream with a small waterfall. THE WORLD, same as film 1 (16:9, warm sand-coloured background). COLOUR MAP reused from film 1: source or starting population GREY; the cause that is changed or selected GOLD; the population after the change TEAL. Guppies are simple cartoon fish, not photographs. Life-history panels are labelled 'schematic'. Numbers appear only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: The seeds that were left are the leading suspect. But nobody can rerun 1977. So how do you test what did the selecting?
scenes.visual: A small recap tile in the corner: film 1's three lamps and the GOLD arrow S over the finch dot plot. A large question mark covers the seed panel labelled 'suspect'. The tile slides away as a stream fades in.
scenes.narration: The seeds that were left are the leading suspect. But nobody can rerun 1977. So how do you test what did the selecting?

scenes.tts: Go to the mountain streams of Trinidad, where guppies live. In some stream reaches, the main predators eat adult guppies. In others, the main fish predator mostly takes small juveniles.
scenes.visual: Two stream reaches side by side, both with GREY guppies. Left reach: a large predator fish with a GOLD outline lunges at an adult guppy; label 'predators of adults'. Right reach: a small predator fish with a GOLD outline chases a tiny juvenile; label 'predator of juveniles'.
scenes.narration: Go to the mountain streams of Trinidad, where guppies live. In some stream reaches, the main predators eat adult guppies. In others, the main fish predator mostly takes small juveniles.

scenes.tts: Guppy populations from the two kinds of site differ in life history. That means when they mature, at what size, and how many young they produce.
scenes.visual: Under each reach a three-row panel labelled 'life history (schematic)': 'age at maturity', 'size at maturity', 'number of young'. Each row has a bar, and the bars differ in length between the two reaches. No numbers on the bars.
scenes.narration: Guppy populations from the two kinds of site differ in life history. That means when they mature, at what size, and how many young they produce.

scenes.tts: So did the predators shape those traits? The pattern fits that idea. But a comparison across natural sites shows only an association, not a cause.
scenes.visual: A GOLD dashed line joins each predator to its life-history panel, with a label 'association'. A stamp 'CAUSE?' hovers and stays unpressed.
scenes.narration: So did the predators shape those traits? The pattern fits that idea. But a comparison across natural sites shows only an association, not a cause.

scenes.tts: The sites differ in other ways too. Stream size, food, light and history all change from one site to the next. Comparing the sites cannot pull those apart.
scenes.visual: Four more labelled icons drift into the gap between the reaches: a ruler 'stream size', a leaf 'food', a sun 'light', a clock 'history'. Each draws its own dashed line to the life-history panels, tangling with the predator lines.
scenes.narration: The sites differ in other ways too. Stream size, food, light and history all change from one site to the next. Comparing the sites cannot pull those apart.

scenes.tts: So change the proposed cause on purpose. Guppies from a site with predators of adults were moved to a site whose predator mostly eats juveniles.
scenes.visual: The rival icons fade. A cartoon net scoops GREY guppies from the left reach and carries them along a GOLD arrow to the right reach, above a waterfall. Label 'moved'.
scenes.narration: So change the proposed cause on purpose. Guppies from a site with predators of adults were moved to a site whose predator mostly eats juveniles.

scenes.tts: The moved population then evolved in its new reach. David Reznick, Heather Bryga and John Endler compared it with its source population eleven years later.
scenes.caption: The moved population then evolved in its new reach. David Reznick, Heather Bryga and John Endler compared it with its source population 11 years later.
scenes.visual: A timeline arrow runs along the bottom from 'moved' to '11 years later'. On-screen under it: '30 to 60 guppy generations'. Small generation ticks flicker past. The moved guppies begin to tint from GREY toward TEAL.
scenes.narration: The moved population then evolved in its new reach. David Reznick, Heather Bryga and John Endler compared it with its source population 11 years later.

scenes.tts: Notice what is different now. The moved guppies and their source started as one population. The researchers made the change, instead of finding sites that already differed.
scenes.visual: Split view: the GREY source population on the left, the TEAL-tinting moved population on the right, joined at the top by a single GREY bracket labelled 'one starting population'. The GOLD arrow between them is labelled 'the change made: a new reach, with a different predator'. The rival icons from scene 5 stay faded in the background, each with a small grey question tag; they are not crossed out.
scenes.narration: Notice what is different now. The moved guppies and their source started as one population. The researchers made the change, instead of finding sites that already differed.

scenes.tts: In the new site, adults are safer and the young are the ones being eaten. Should the moved guppies now mature earlier, or later?
scenes.visual: Right reach close-up: the juvenile predator, a few TEAL-tinted adults swimming freely. Question card: 'Mature earlier or later?'
scenes.narration: In the new site, adults are safer and the young are the ones being eaten. Should the moved guppies now mature earlier, or later?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds. A 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: Later, and at a larger size. The moved population had changed its life history in the direction life-history theory predicted. It matched the natural comparison.
scenes.visual: The moved population's life-history panel turns fully TEAL: the 'age at maturity' and 'size at maturity' bars grow longer, labelled 'later' and 'larger'. A GREY copy of the source panel sits beside it for comparison. A small check mark links the TEAL panel to the natural right-reach panel from scene 3.
scenes.narration: Later, and at a larger size. The moved population had changed its life history in the direction life-history theory predicted. It matched the natural comparison.

scenes.tts: A manipulation can rule out some explanations that an observation leaves open. But this is still one stream and one introduction. And the new reach differed in more than its predator. So it showed that the change of setting caused evolution more firmly than it showed exactly how.
scenes.visual: A stamp 'CHANGE TESTED' presses onto the GOLD arrow. Then two small caution tags appear beside it: 'one stream, one introduction' and 'new reach differs in more than predator'; the faded rival icons pulse once.
scenes.narration: A manipulation can rule out some explanations that an observation leaves open. But this is still one stream and one introduction. And the new reach differed in more than its predator. So it showed that the change of setting caused evolution more firmly than it showed exactly how.

scenes.tts: So there are three tools, each for its own question. Observation of natural variation shows an association. An experimental contrast tests a cause, because the cause was changed on purpose.
scenes.visual: Three tool cards stand side by side at the same height, none above another. Left, GREY: a naturalist with a notebook, 'observation: association'. Middle, GOLD: an experimenter with a net, 'experimental contrast: tests a cause'. Right card stays dim.
scenes.narration: So there are three tools, each for its own question. Observation of natural variation shows an association. An experimental contrast tests a cause, because the cause was changed on purpose.

scenes.tts: But nobody can move a past event. That needs the third tool. Historical inference tests rival explanations against the traces the past has left. Each tool answers a different question.
scenes.visual: The right card lights TEAL: a detective with a magnifying glass, 'historical inference: tests rival pasts against traces'. All three cards glow together at equal height.
scenes.narration: But nobody can move a past event. That needs the third tool. Historical inference tests rival explanations against the traces the past has left. Each tool answers a different question.

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot. Take-home line: 'Changing a cause on purpose tests what a comparison only suggests.'
